text:
nora: Hey team — spotted a weird one while migrating a consumer app to yarn berry (pnp) that imports @redwood/sdk. Local dev (node) is fine but the edge build (Vercel Edge) fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED for deep import like `@redwood/sdk/lib/runtime`. Also TS in the consumer resolves to the raw src via paths mapping and picks up internal private types instead of dist d.ts. Anyone seen deep-import + pnp + exports mismatch?

diego: yeah been there. With `exports` set in package.json, deep subpath imports (./lib/*) are blocked unless you explicitly export them. Many teams rely on deep imports in examples which makes the published package behave different from workspace. What's your package.json exports field?

nora: it's minimal: "exports": {"import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js"} — nothing for subpaths. Our consumer used `import { createClient } from "@redwood/sdk/lib/runtime"` because older examples referenced internal helpers.

mei: oh that will fail with node/edge when bundlers honor exports; pnp makes it stricter too. Two options: (A) stop deep imports in consumers and add a compat layer in SDK that re-exports public APIs from the top-level index, or (B) add explicit subpath exports you want to support, e.g. "./lib/runtime": {"import":"./dist/lib/runtime.mjs","require":"./dist/lib/runtime.cjs","types":"./dist/lib/runtime.d.ts"}.

nora: Hmm, the consumer is a bunch of internal apps across the org, so breaking deep imports is a big diff. Adding subpath exports seems better. But TS still resolves to src not dist in some editors.

diego: For TS in monorepos, watch out for tsconfig `paths` and Yarn PnP virtual filesystem — tsserver may prefer workspace source if `references` or path mapping points to `packages/sdk/src`. Make sure your build publishes `dist` and that package.json `types` points to `dist/index.d.ts`. Also remove any accidental `exports` that point to src.

nora: We have types: "dist/index.d.ts". However some consumers have a root tsconfig with `paths: {"@redwood/sdk": ["packages/sdk/src"]}` for in-repo development. That explains editor choosing src. Any low-friction fixes?

olga: Two pragmatic approaches: (1) CI + dev scripts: have a `postbuild:examples` script that copies `dist/package.json` and `dist/` artifacts into a temporary example app that simulates how the package will be consumed when published, and run tsserver against it in CI to catch these mismatch problems. (2) add a `prepare` script in the SDK that runs on `yarn install` in workspace to generate a minimal published-like layout in dist (copy package.json, README, types). That helps PnP and bundlers behave like published package.

mei: Also consider adding `exports` "./package.json": "./package.json" if you rely on reading package.json from consumers. Some bundlers block access otherwise. And include `files` array to list dist so pack/publish includes only what's needed.

nora: Good tip about ./package.json export. The edge bundler error happens only after switching consumer from `require('@redwood/sdk')` to ESM `import` and upgrading the bundler; older CJS builds silently fell back. The real runtime error: `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: Package subpath './lib/runtime' is not defined by "exports"`

diego: Yup. If you want to be conservative, add a `compat` entry point that re-exports legacy internal modules and mark it as deprecated. E.g., `import { legacyRuntime } from './dist/compat/legacy.js'` and export it at "./compat/*" subpath. Then you can run a scheduled cleanup to remove compat later.

nora: We'll do subpath exports + compat layer. One more hiccup: consumers on Yarn PnP report the editor still complains about missing d.ts for the compat subpath. Is there a way to hint tsserver to prefer the `types` in exports?

mei: You can add the `types` condition inside each export mapping: "./compat/legacy": {"types":"./dist/compat/legacy.d.ts","import":"./dist/compat/legacy.mjs"}. Some tools read that. For tsserver specifically, `typesVersions` works as a fallback: "typesVersions": {"*": {"*": ["dist/*"]}} although it's coarse. Another trick: ship `dist/index.d.ts` at top-level and ensure it's the one referenced by `types` field; tsserver then picks it up even in many pnp setups.

olga: And for Yarn PnP you can add a `.yarnrc.yml` workspace protocol mapping to prefer the built package in dev if you want to avoid editing many consumers. But that is more invasive.

nora: OK, plan: add explicit subpath exports for compat, include `types` per export, add `./package.json` export, and add a `prepare` script to copy package.json into dist on installs. I'll open a PR with those changes plus a small examples/compat-app to validate.

diego: Also add a CI job that runs the edge bundler against examples using both pnpm and yarn (classic/berry) to catch env-specific resolution. We added that months back and it caught several regressions.

ci-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/563 for subpath exports + pnp compat and scheduled CI matrix job.

mei: One last gotcha we hit: when supporting both CJS and ESM you may accidentally ship dual entry files that re-export with different shapes (named vs default). Consumers using `import * as sdk from '@redwood/sdk'` vs `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'` can break depending on interop. Add clear READMEs and test both import styles in your examples.

nora: Great point — we'll add unit tests that import via both styles and exercise compatibility mode. Thanks all — PR will reference this thread when opened.

olga: TL;DR: deep imports blocked by `exports` + PnP stricter resolution; fix by adding subpath exports or a compat re-export, include types in exports and/or use typesVersions, ship dist/package.json via prepare, and add CI checks for pnpm/yarn + edge bundlers.

nora: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1044 — includes compat layer, exports updates, types per export, and examples/compat-app. Will follow up once CI runs.
